record.notes: Released by the Digital Policy Office on 15 Apr 2025; the current text is version 1.1 (December 2025). The DPO commissioned the Hong Kong Generative AI Research and Development Center (HKGAI), established in 2023 with AIR@InnoHK funding, to study and suggest codes and guidelines, and promulgated the guideline after considering its findings; it says it will update the guideline regularly. Where the Chinese and English versions differ, the English version prevails. It is published on the same DPO page as the Ethical AI Framework (HK-01).

verification.note: Recheck of 18 Oct 2026. Stored and read: the Digital Policy Office's page 'AI and Data Ethics' (digitalpolicy.gov.hk, copy of 11 Oct 2026, re-checked unchanged on 18 Oct 2026), which says the DPO commissioned HKGAI and promulgated the guideline, and links its PDF; the guideline PDF, version 1.1 dated December 2025 (copy of 11 Oct 2026, unchanged on 18 Oct 2026), with its preamble, the technical limitations and service risks, the four-tier risk classification, the five dimensions of governance and the practical guidance for technology developers, service providers and users; and the HKSAR Government press release of 15 Apr 2025 (info.gov.hk, 18 Oct 2026), 'Digital Policy Office releases Hong Kong Generative Artificial Intelligence Technical and Application Guideline', which dates the release to 15 Apr 2025. date_published, empty in the earlier record, now follows the press release. The PDF has no version history, so what changed in version 1.1 is not stated.

notes.quote: The Digital Policy Office (DPO) released today (April 15) the Hong Kong Generative Artificial Intelligence Technical and Application Guideline (the Guideline).
Established in 2023 with funding from the AIR@InnoHK, which focuses on AI and robotics technology, the HKGAI focuses on the research and development (R&D) of generative AI technology
The office will regularly update the Guideline for reference by all sectors.
In the event of any discrepancies between the Chinese and English versions of this document, please refer to the English version and notify the Digital Policy Office.

summary.quote: The proposed AI governance framework establishes a four-tiered risk classification system, creating a proportionate governance approach based on potential harm.
High-risk AI-generated content, such as deepfakes, ID document images, and financial materials, should include irremovable watermarks or embedded codes
they should hire independent auditors to regularly audit the quality, safety, and compliance of the services
The degree of human oversight should be based on the impact of different stages

judgment.status_reasoning: The DPO page (re-checked unchanged on 18 Oct 2026) presents the guideline as promulgated by the DPO and links version 1.1 of December 2025; the preamble calls it codes and practices for reference by various sectors and says the DPO will update it regularly. It is non-binding guidance; nothing stored shows a later version or a withdrawal. 'Published (non-binding, current)' and 'Non-binding' stand.
judgment.date_reasoning: date_published 2025-04-15: the press release says the DPO 'released today (April 15)' the guideline and is dated Tuesday, April 15, 2025. date_last_updated 2025-12 is version 1.1's date, given only as 'December 2025'.
judgment.scope_reasoning: Government guidance on the risks and governance of generative AI for developers, service providers and users; in scope with no note.
judgment.summary_reasoning: Each claim was checked against version 1.1: hallucination, bias, deepfakes, jailbreaks and data leakage as risks; five dimensions of governance; the four risk tiers; watermarks for high-risk content; independent audits; risk assessments at stages of service development; human oversight proportionate to impact. The summary is kept.
